question: Java 21: Customer overrides equals(Object) to compare customerId. What must a compatible hashCode() guarantee?
correct_option: Objects equal by customerId produce the same hash code.
distractors: Objects with different customerIds always produce different hash codes.
Objects equal by customerId retain identity-based hash codes.
Objects equal by customerId may produce different hash codes.
explanation:
Equality requires matching hashes. Unequal objects may share a hash, so uniqueness is not required. Identity-based hashing is not automatically compatible with value equality; equal objects cannot have different hashes.

Source: [Object contract, Java 21](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/21/docs/api/java.base/java/lang/Object.html#hashCode()).

question: Java 21: Two unequal keys have the same hash code. What happens when both are inserted into a HashMap?
correct_option: Both mappings can remain stored; equality distinguishes the keys.
distractors: Only the latest mapping remains stored; matching hashes make keys equal.
The second insertion is rejected; matching hashes are invalid.
Both mappings remain stored; lookups distinguish keys by identity only.
explanation:
A collision does not make keys equal or prohibit insertion. Equality can distinguish colliding keys; lookup is not limited to reference identity.

Source: [HashMap, Java 21](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/21/docs/api/java.base/java/util/HashMap.html).

question: Java 21: scores is a HashMap<String, Integer>. scores.get("sam") returns null. Which check distinguishes a missing key from a key mapped to null?
correct_option: Use scores.containsKey("sam"); it checks whether that key is present.
distractors: Use scores.get("sam") == null; it checks whether that key is absent.
Use scores.isEmpty(); it checks whether this particular key is absent.
Use scores.containsValue(null); it checks whether this key maps to null.
explanation:
get can return null in both cases. containsKey distinguishes them. isEmpty describes the entire map, and containsValue cannot identify a particular key.

Source: [HashMap.get, Java 21](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/21/docs/api/java.base/java/util/HashMap.html#get(java.lang.Object)).

question: Java 21: CustomerKey equality and hashing use mutable customerId. After insertion, customerId changes. Which design change best keeps map lookups reliable?
correct_option: Use keys whose equality and hash fields remain stable while stored.
distractors: Recompute hashCode on lookup so the stored entry moves between buckets.
Make customerId volatile so the stored entry follows key mutations.
Increase initial capacity so mutations cannot affect bucket lookup.
explanation:
Map behavior is unspecified after equality-affecting key mutations. Recomputing a hash does not relocate an entry. Visibility from volatile and extra capacity do not keep the key's equality stable.

Source: [Mutable map keys, Java 21](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/21/docs/api/java.base/java/util/Map.html).
